Answer: B
Reason: The clinical presentation of persistent parenchymal consolidation (infiltration) in the left lower lobe that does not resolve, combined with the specific absence of hilar or mediastinal lymphadenopathy on imaging (as seen in the CT scan, Figure 2), is a classic description used to differentiate Bronchiolitis obliterans organizing pneumonia (BOOP/COP) from malignancy or other infectious etiologies.
